Hi Samir / Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

What you told us:
- Workload: real-time payment fraud scoring integrated into checkout; ~150 tokens per request (feature vector + prompt).
- Traffic profile: sustained 200 qps, peak ~350 qps during spikes, ~6M calls/day.
- Latency targets: p50 ~ <=50ms, p95 <=200ms — p99 is less critical but would like to avoid >500ms tails.
- Reliability: must maintain service during peak windows and have predictable latency for SLAs.
- Timeline / procurement: pilot in next 4–6 weeks; procurement decision by end of Q3.

Our initial guidance:
- Hosted API is fastest to start (no infra setup) and works well for lower steady-state throughput. However, given your sustained 200 qps with 350 qps peaks and tight p50/p95 targets, you’ll likely get the most predictable tail latency and throughput with Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity).
- Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools, predictable batching and KV cache behavior, and SLA-backed latency. It also unlocks configurable autoscaling and burst policies that match your traffic profile.

Proposed next steps:
1) Neha (SE) to run a short benchmark on a sample payload to validate latency at 200–350 qps and provide a recommended Dedicated pod size.
2) We can run a 2–3 week pilot on Hosted with cooperative rate limits if you want to start integration quickly while Dedicated contract is finalized.
3) I’ll follow up with a short scope doc and pricing summary (attached).

I’ve attached the requirements spreadsheet from today — please flag anything I missed.

Thanks,

Thanks for the context — ran an initial sizing check and wrote up recommendations below. I’ll attach the detailed benchmark plan and our Dedicated pricing PDF.

Summary recommendation (short): Dedicated capacity recommended for production. Rationale: your sustained 200 qps (350 qps peaks) with a tight p50 target requires isolated GPUs and predictable batching behavior that Hosted cannot guarantee at scale. Dedicated also reduces noisy-neighbor variability and supports autoscaling policies that keep p95 within your SLA.

Suggested starting config:
- Dedicated pods: 2 pods (primary + hot standby/burst) each sized to handle ~200 qps of 150-token requests with headroom for batching. This gives capacity for sustained load and room for spikes (we can tune autoscaling to add more pods during sustained peaks).
- Expected latency (estimate from similar workloads): p50 ~ 30–55ms, p95 ~ 120–220ms depending on prompt complexity and batch tuning. We should run the benchmark to tighten these bands.
- Migration path: start PoC on Hosted for integration/fallback within 2 weeks. Provision Dedicated env in parallel (2–3 week lead time depending on contract). Cutover via DNS switch + gradual traffic ramp (can do A/B or canary).

Cost / next steps:
- I attached our Dedicated pricing sheet (redwood_dedicated_pricing_2026.pdf) and a bench plan. Ballpark: mid-five-figure monthly range depending on exact pod spec and commit term. I’ll produce a 1-page recommendation for Samir that includes suggested pod sizes, expected latency bands, and a migration timeline.
- Action items: Aditya to confirm PoC start date; Samir to share sample payloads/test tokenization; Marissa to drive procurement timeline and next call.
